## Q ai-20261022-a21-11
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.1
- topic: integration
- services: Amazon MQ, SQS, SNS, EC2
- tags: decoupling
- difficulty: easy
- skills: 2.1.k2, 2.1.s7
- concept: Amazon MQ is the managed broker for applications that rely on JMS and ActiveMQ protocols, avoiding code changes and broker administration
- refs: 07-application-integration.md
- hint: Giữ nguyên JMS/OpenWire và mã nguồn, không muốn vá lỗi máy chủ broker — dịch vụ message nào được quản lý hộ mà vẫn nói đúng giao thức đó?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 105

A logistics company runs an order-routing application on premises that exchanges messages with an Apache ActiveMQ broker by using the JMS API and the OpenWire protocol. The company is moving the application to Amazon EC2 and wants to stop patching and operating broker servers while keeping the application code and messaging protocol unchanged. The broker must stay available if an Availability Zone fails. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Replace the broker with Amazon SQS standard queues and rewrite the messaging code of the application to use the AWS SDK for queue operations.
- B. Create an Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ broker with an active/standby deployment across two Availability Zones and point the application at its endpoint.
- C. Install Apache ActiveMQ on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones with a shared Amazon EFS file system.
- D. Replace the broker with an Amazon SNS topic and subscribe the application's HTTPS endpoints so that messages are pushed to the application.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** Amazon MQ runs a managed ActiveMQ broker that existing applications use without rewriting messaging code, and an active/standby deployment puts the standby in a second Availability Zone while AWS handles patching.
- SQS with an SDK rewrite: requires application code changes (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- ActiveMQ on EC2 with EFS: patching, failover, and capacity stay with the team (tốn vận hành hơn)
- SNS topic: a push pub/sub service with neither JMS queues nor OpenWire (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazon-mq/latest/developer-guide/amazon-mq-broker-architecture.html
> 🇻🇳 Giữ nguyên JMS/OpenWire, bỏ việc quản trị broker → Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ) active/standby đa AZ; SQS/SNS buộc sửa code.

## Q ai-20261022-a21-18
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.1
- topic: compute
- services: EC2 Auto Scaling, EBS, ALB
- tags: asg-warm-pool, scaling-policies, launch-template
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 2.1.k6, 2.1.s2
- concept: A warm pool of stopped, pre-initialized instances cuts scale-out latency for slow-booting instances at a cost of EBS only, unlike scheduled scaling, timer tweaks, or a peak-sized minimum
- refs: 01-compute-services.md, C-kien-truc-web-app.md
- hint: Boot mất chừng mười phút, tải tăng bất ngờ nên không đặt lịch được và không muốn chạy sẵn cả ngày — làm sao có sẵn máy đã khởi tạo mà rẻ?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 145

A genomics SaaS company runs a web application on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Each new instance downloads a large reference dataset to its EBS root volume and builds caches during boot, which takes about ten minutes before the instance passes load balancer health checks. Request volume rises sharply and unpredictably several times a day, and users see timeouts while new instances are still starting. Keeping the group scaled for the peak all day would be too expensive. Which solution will reduce the scale-out delay MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Reduce the health check grace period and the scaling cooldown of the Auto Scaling group so that new instances are launched and registered with the load balancer sooner.
- B. Add a warm pool of pre-initialized instances in the Stopped state and use a lifecycle hook to finish initialization before the instances stop.
- C. Configure scheduled scaling actions that add capacity at the times of day when the traffic spikes usually occur, based on the graphs of last week.
- D. Raise the minimum capacity of the group to the number of instances that the peak needs so that enough instances are running through the whole day.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** A warm pool keeps initialized instances stopped, so scale-out starts from a prepared instance instead of a ten-minute boot, and stopped instances cost only for their EBS volumes.
- Shorter grace period and cooldown: they do not shorten the boot time of an instance (dùng sai tính năng)
- Scheduled scaling: the spikes are unpredictable, so no schedule matches them (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Minimum capacity at peak: keeps peak capacity running all day (tốn chi phí hơn)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-warm-pools.html
> 🇻🇳 Instance khởi động lâu + tải bất ngờ + tiết kiệm → warm pool (instance đã khởi tạo ở trạng thái Stopped, chỉ trả phí EBS).

## Q ai-20261022-a21-23
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.1
- topic: compute
- services: Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, SES, EC2, Fargate
- tags: serverless-cost
- difficulty: easy
- skills: 2.1.k12, 2.1.s5
- concept: Bursty, rare, short work with no operations staff fits Lambda with API Gateway because it bills only while requests run and needs no capacity planning
- refs: 01-compute-services.md, C-kien-truc-web-app.md
- hint: Tải rải rác theo đợt, mỗi lần chỉ vài giây, không có đội vận hành — mô hình tính phí nào chỉ trả khi có xử lý?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 120

A small online-learning company creates a student profile and sends a welcome email each time a student registers through a web form. Registrations arrive in short bursts after marketing campaigns and are rare otherwise, and each registration needs about two seconds of processing. The company has no operations staff and wants to pay only while registrations are processed, with no servers to manage and no capacity to plan. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Run the code that creates the profile and sends the welcome email on two Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
- B. Run the code that creates the profile and sends the welcome email as an Amazon ECS service on AWS Fargate with a minimum of one task behind an Application Load Balancer.
- C. Expose an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API that invokes an AWS Lambda function, which writes the profile to DynamoDB and sends the email by using SES.
- D. Run the code that creates the profile and sends the welcome email on one Amazon EC2 instance that is covered by a one-year Savings Plan to lower its hourly price.

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** Lambda behind API Gateway bills for requests and run time, scales through bursts, and needs no servers, so idle periods cost almost nothing.
- EC2 Auto Scaling group with ALB: instances and a load balancer bill around the clock (tốn chi phí hơn)
- Fargate with one minimum task: a task and a load balancer run even when idle (tốn chi phí hơn)
- One instance with a Savings Plan: a commitment on idle capacity that still needs patching (tốn vận hành hơn)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/welcome.html
> 🇻🇳 Tải rải rác, ngắn, không có đội vận hành, chỉ muốn trả khi có xử lý → Lambda + API Gateway; EC2/Fargate tối thiểu vẫn tính tiền khi rảnh.

## Q ai-20261022-a21-26
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.1
- topic: compute
- services: EC2 Auto Scaling, SQS, CloudWatch
- tags: scaling-policies, decoupling
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 2.1.s2, 2.1.k6
- concept: Scale queue workers with target tracking on a backlog-per-instance metric derived from acceptable latency and processing time, not on CPU, raw queue length, or a fixed schedule
- refs: C-kien-truc-web-app.md, 07-application-integration.md
- hint: CPU thấp vì worker chờ API ngoài trong khi hàng đợi dài ra — chỉ số nào tỉ lệ với việc đang chờ trên mỗi instance?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 135

A photo-printing company runs worker instances in an Auto Scaling group that pull print jobs from an Amazon SQS queue. Job arrival rates change unpredictably during the day, and the average processing time per job is a stable 6 seconds. The company wants jobs to wait no longer than about 2 minutes, without keeping unused instances. The group scales on average CPU utilization, which stays low even when the backlog grows because workers spend most of their time waiting on a slow third-party API. Which scaling approach will meet these requirements?

- A. Use a target tracking policy on the ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric of the queue with a fixed backlog target that ignores the number of instances and the processing time of the jobs.
- B. Use a target tracking policy on a backlog-per-instance metric, calculated as queue length divided by in-service instances, with a target based on acceptable latency and job processing time.
- C. Use a scheduled scaling action that doubles the desired capacity of the group every morning and halves it every evening to follow the average daily pattern of jobs.
- D. Lower the CPU target value of the existing target tracking policy so that the group scales out at a lower average CPU utilization of the instances that process a job.

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** Backlog per instance scales the fleet with the waiting work, using a target of acceptable latency divided by processing time (here 120 s ÷ 6 s = 20 messages), independent of CPU.
- Raw queue length: ignores the number of running instances and can over-scale while the queue drains (dùng sai tính năng)
- Scheduled scaling: arrival rates are unpredictable, so a schedule cannot track them (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Lower CPU target: CPU stays low while workers wait on the API, so it is the wrong signal (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html
> 🇻🇳 Worker đọc SQS, CPU thấp giả → target tracking theo "backlog per instance" (độ dài hàng đợi ÷ số instance), đích = độ trễ chấp nhận ÷ thời gian xử lý.

## Q ai-20261022-a21-33
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.1
- topic: networking
- services: CloudFront, Global Accelerator, NLB, ALB, S3, Route 53
- tags: route53-health-checks, high-availability
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 2.1.k7, 2.1.s6
- concept: CloudFront accelerates cacheable HTTP content; Global Accelerator gives static anycast IPs and fast health-based failover for UDP/TCP endpoints; DNS routing and wrong pairings fail the stated constraints
- refs: 04-networking-services.md, 14-so-sanh-services.md
- hint: Một phần HTTPS cache được, một phần UDP cần IP cố định và chuyển vùng trong vài giây — mỗi loại traffic hợp dịch vụ tăng tốc biên nào?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 170

A multiplayer game company serves two kinds of traffic from AWS. A web portal and its marketing images are delivered over HTTPS from an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. Real-time game sessions run on dedicated servers behind Network Load Balancers in three Regions and use UDP. Players' firewalls allow-list a fixed set of IP addresses, and sessions must fail over to another Region within seconds when a Region becomes unhealthy. The company wants better performance for players worldwide for both kinds of traffic. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket and the ALB as origins to cache the portal content close to players.
- B. Create a CloudFront distribution with the three NLBs as origins so that the UDP game sessions travel through CloudFront edge locations to the servers.
- C. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator with the S3 bucket as an endpoint so that the portal images are cached at the edge.
- D. Create Route 53 latency-based records with health checks for the three NLBs and let player clients resolve the nearest healthy Region through DNS with a short TTL.
- E. Create a Global Accelerator standard accelerator with UDP listeners and an endpoint group in each Region that holds the NLB.

**Answer:** A, E

**Explanation:** CloudFront caches the HTTPS portal content at the edge, and Global Accelerator gives UDP traffic static anycast IP addresses and health-based failover across Regions.
- CloudFront for game sessions: it serves HTTP and HTTPS, not UDP (dùng sai tính năng)
- Global Accelerator with an S3 endpoint: it does not cache, and S3 is not an endpoint type (cấu hình không tồn tại)
- Route 53 latency records: DNS caching delays failover and gives no fixed IPs (vi phạm ràng buộc)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-components.html
> 🇻🇳 Web HTTPS cache được → CloudFront; UDP + IP cố định + failover vùng trong vài giây → Global Accelerator (listener UDP, endpoint là NLB); DNS không đủ nhanh.

## Q ai-20261022-a22-01
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.2
- topic: resilience
- services: DynamoDB, EC2 Auto Scaling, ALB, Route 53, AWS Backup, CloudFormation
- tags: dr-pilot-light, rto-rpo, dynamodb-global-tables, multi-region
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 2.2.k4, 2.2.s6
- concept: Pilot light is the cheapest DR strategy that meets an RPO of seconds when the RTO allows an hour of downtime
- refs: A-nen-tang-kien-truc.md, P-architecture-diagrams.md
- hint: RPO vài giây loại sao lưu theo giờ; RTO một giờ cho phép chưa bật phần tính toán — chọn mức rẻ nhất vẫn đạt cả hai.
- family: dr-strategy-qualifier
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 140

A ride-sharing company runs its trip-booking API in us-east-1 on an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances fronted by an Application Load Balancer, with trip data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Client traffic is routed by Amazon Route 53. The company is designing disaster recovery in us-west-2 in case us-east-1 becomes unavailable. The business accepts up to one hour of downtime but only a few seconds of data loss. The application tier is stateless, and its AMIs and infrastructure are defined in AWS CloudFormation templates. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Schedule hourly AWS Backup copies of the DynamoDB table and the AMIs to us-west-2, then run the CloudFormation templates, restore the table, and update the Route 53 record after a disaster
- B. Add a us-west-2 replica to form a global table and copy the AMIs, then launch the load balancer and Auto Scaling group from CloudFormation and update Route 53 once a disaster is declared
- C. Add a us-west-2 replica to form a global table, run a minimum-size Auto Scaling group behind a load balancer, and fail over with Route 53 and scale out when a disaster is declared
- D. Add a us-west-2 replica to form a global table, run full-capacity stacks in both Regions, and use Route 53 latency records with health checks to serve users from the closest healthy Region

**Answer:** B

**Explanation:** A global table keeps the DR copy current within seconds, and since an hour of downtime is acceptable, compute can stay switched off until a disaster is declared (pilot light), the cheapest design meeting the RPO.
- Hourly AWS Backup copies: up to an hour of data loss instead of seconds (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- Minimum-size group always running: meets the goals but pays for compute that a one-hour RTO does not need (tốn chi phí hơn).
- Full-capacity stacks in both Regions: near-zero RTO nobody asked for, at the highest cost (tốn chi phí hơn).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html
> 🇻🇳 RPO vài giây + RTO 1 giờ → pilot light: chỉ nhân bản dữ liệu liên tục, phần tính toán bật khi có thảm hoạ.

## Q ai-20261022-a22-09
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.2
- topic: resilience
- services: AWS Backup, Organizations, EBS, RDS, EFS
- tags: automated-backups, multi-region, cross-account-access, snapshots
- difficulty: hard
- skills: 2.2.s5, 2.2.s1
- concept: AWS Backup Organizations policies, cross-account backup, and a logically air-gapped vault protect backups from a compromised account
- refs: 13-other-services.md, B-bao-mat-compliance.md
- hint: Cần ba mảnh ghép: chính sách áp tự động cho cả tổ chức, cho phép chép sang tài khoản khác, và kho đích mà tài khoản bị chiếm không xoá được.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 180

A retailer runs workloads in 25 AWS accounts managed with AWS Organizations. Amazon EBS volumes, Amazon RDS databases, and Amazon EFS file systems must be backed up daily and retained for 90 days. After a ransomware scare, the security team requires a copy of every backup in a second Region and in a separate backup account, stored in a vault that attackers who compromise a workload account cannot delete. The same policy must apply automatically to new accounts. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose THREE)

- A. Create an AWS Organizations backup policy that defines a daily plan with 90-day retention and a copy action, and attach it to the organization root
- B. Configure a local backup plan in each workload account of the organization and copy the recovery points to the backup account manually with the AWS CLI after each daily job
- C. Create a logically air-gapped vault in the backup account in the second Region and use it as the copy destination
- D. Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication to a second Region on the buckets that hold exported snapshots and apply S3 Object Lock in governance mode
- E. Store the backups in a standard vault in each workload account and attach an IAM policy that denies the delete actions
- F. Enable cross-account backup in the AWS Backup settings of the management account so that member accounts can copy recovery points to other accounts

**Answer:** A, C, F

**Explanation:** An Organizations backup policy applies the plan and copy action to every account, including new ones; cross-account backup lets copies leave the account, and a logically air-gapped vault is locked, so a compromised workload account cannot delete its recovery points.
- Local plans with manual CLI copies: no automatic coverage of new accounts and more work (tốn vận hành hơn).
- S3 replication and Object Lock: these protect S3 objects, not EBS, RDS, or EFS recovery points (giải bài toán khác).
- Standard vault with an IAM deny: an administrator of a compromised account can remove it (dùng sai tính năng).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/logicallyairgappedvault.html
> 🇻🇳 Backup chống ransomware đa tài khoản: Organizations backup policy + bật cross-account + vault air-gapped ở tài khoản backup, khác Region.

## Q ai-20261022-a22-13
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.2
- topic: networking
- services: Route 53, ALB, Global Accelerator, CloudFront
- tags: route53-routing, route53-health-checks, alias-records, multi-region
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 2.2.k1, 2.2.k6
- concept: Route 53 failover alias records with Evaluate Target Health are the cheapest automatic active-passive Regional failover
- refs: 04-networking-services.md
- hint: Cần chuyển Region tự động, không phụ thuộc Region chính, và rẻ nhất — loại giải pháp có phí cố định hoặc không xử lý được POST.

A gaming company serves a REST API at api.example.com from Application Load Balancers in two Regions: us-east-1 is primary and eu-west-1 is a warm standby. Most requests are HTTPS POST calls. The company wants traffic to move to the standby Region automatically when the primary Region's load balancer becomes unhealthy, and the move must not depend on any resource in the primary Region. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

- A. Create Route 53 primary and secondary failover alias records that point to the two load balancers, with Evaluate Target Health turned on for both records
- B. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator with one endpoint group per Region that contains the matching load balancer, and let its health checks shift connections
- C. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin group that uses the primary load balancer as the primary origin and the standby load balancer as the secondary origin
- D. Create Route 53 weighted records, and run an AWS Lambda function in us-east-1 that sets the primary Region's weight to zero when a CloudWatch alarm fires

**Answer:** A

**Explanation:** Failover alias records with Evaluate Target Health follow the load balancers' own health, send answers to the standby when the primary is unhealthy, and run on Route 53's data plane without relying on the primary Region; no separate health check fee applies.
- Global Accelerator: also meets the goals but adds a fixed hourly fee plus a data transfer premium (tốn chi phí hơn).
- CloudFront origin group: fails over only GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS requests, not the POST calls (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- Lambda in us-east-1 changing weights: depends on the primary Region and on control-plane calls (vi phạm ràng buộc).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html
> 🇻🇳 Active-passive rẻ nhất, không phụ thuộc Region chính → Route 53 failover alias + Evaluate Target Health.

## Q ai-20261022-a22-20
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.2
- topic: networking
- services: NAT Gateway, VPC, Internet Gateway
- tags: subnets, high-availability, egress-only-igw
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 2.2.k3, 2.2.s4
- concept: A NAT gateway is resilient only inside its Availability Zone, so each zone needs its own gateway and a route table pointing to it
- refs: 04-networking-services.md
- hint: Một NAT gateway chỉ chịu lỗi trong AZ của nó — cần cả tài nguyên mỗi AZ lẫn bảng định tuyến trỏ đúng NAT cùng AZ.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 135

A company runs application servers in private subnets in three Availability Zones. All three private subnets share one route table whose default route points to a single NAT gateway in a public subnet in us-east-1a. The servers call external payment APIs. During an outage of us-east-1a, servers in all three zones lost outbound internet access. The company wants to remove this single point of failure while avoiding cross-zone dependencies. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose TWO)

- A. Add a second NAT gateway to the public subnet in the same Availability Zone and configure equal-cost multipath routing in the route table between the two gateways
- B. Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet in each Availability Zone that contains private subnets
- C. Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance in an Auto Scaling group of size one in us-east-1a
- D. Create a route table for each private subnet that sends 0.0.0.0/0 to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone
- E. Create an egress-only internet gateway and route 0.0.0.0/0 from the private subnets to it

**Answer:** B, D

**Explanation:** A NAT gateway is resilient only within its own Availability Zone, so each zone needs its own gateway, and each private subnet's route table must send the default route to the same-zone gateway.
- Second gateway in one zone with multipath routing: a route has a single target and both gateways fail together (cấu hình không tồn tại).
- NAT instance in a one-instance group in us-east-1a: still one zone, plus patching work (tốn vận hành hơn).
- Egress-only internet gateway: outbound access for IPv6 only, not IPv4 NAT (dùng sai tính năng).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-scenarios.html
> 🇻🇳 NAT gateway chỉ chịu lỗi trong 1 AZ → mỗi AZ một NAT gateway + route table từng AZ trỏ về NAT cùng AZ.

## Q ai-20261022-a22-33
- domain: resilient
- task: 2.2
- topic: database
- services: ElastiCache, EC2 Auto Scaling, ALB, S3, EBS
- tags: redis-vs-memcached, multi-az, high-availability
- difficulty: medium
- skills: 2.2.k5, 2.2.s4
- concept: A stateless web tier keeps session state in a Multi-AZ ElastiCache replication group instead of instance memory with sticky sessions
- refs: 03-database-services.md, C-kien-truc-web-app.md
- hint: Giỏ hàng nằm trong RAM từng instance nên mất khi scale-in hoặc lỗi — đưa trạng thái ra một kho dùng chung, nhanh và chịu lỗi AZ.
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 110

An online ticketing site runs a stateful PHP application on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions enabled. Sessions are stored in each instance's memory. During Auto Scaling scale-in events and instance failures, customers lose their shopping carts and are signed out. The company wants carts to survive instance failures and scale-in with the lowest latency and minimal code changes; the framework supports external session handlers. Which solution meets these requirements?

- A. Increase the sticky session duration on the load balancer and turn on scale-in protection for the Auto Scaling group so that instances are not terminated
- B. Store each session as an object in Amazon S3 through the framework's session handler and have the application read and write it on every request
- C. Store the sessions on an Amazon EBS volume attached to each instance, point the session handler at it, and snapshot the volumes every five minutes
- D. Store the sessions in an Amazon ElastiCache replication group with Multi-AZ automatic failover and use the framework's session handler

**Answer:** D

**Explanation:** Moving session state out of the instances makes the web tier stateless; an ElastiCache replication group gives in-memory speed, survives web instance failures and scale-in, and with Multi-AZ automatic failover protects the cache itself; framework session handlers need only configuration.
- Longer stickiness with scale-in protection: stickiness still ties a user to one instance, and protection does not help when it fails (dùng sai tính năng).
- Per-request session objects in S3: durable, but every request pays object-store latency (vi phạm ràng buộc).
- Instance-attached EBS with snapshots: volumes go with the instance and snapshots lag minutes (đặt sai chỗ).
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/AutoFailover.html
> 🇻🇳 Web tier phải stateless: session ra ElastiCache (Multi-AZ) thay vì RAM instance + sticky session.

## Q ai-20261022-a34-03
- domain: performance

- concept: Standard VPN tunnels are limited in throughput; aggregating several VPN connections needs a transit gateway with BGP and ECMP, which a virtual private gateway, static routing or acceleration cannot provide
- refs: 04-networking-services.md, 14-so-sanh-services.md
- hint: Mỗi tunnel VPN có trần băng thông — chỉ một loại gateway cộng gộp được nhiều tunnel, và nó đòi hỏi kiểu định tuyến nào?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 135

A company connects its data center to AWS with a Site-to-Site VPN that terminates on a virtual private gateway. A new nightly replication job needs about 4 Gbps of throughput to workloads in VPCs that belong to three accounts, but one VPN connection carries far less than that. A Direct Connect connection will not be ready for several months, and the company's router supports BGP. The company wants the interim connection to carry the load and reach all three VPCs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Create several VPN connections to the virtual private gateway and rely on the gateway to spread the traffic across the tunnels.
- B. Create two VPN connections to a transit gateway that use static routes instead of BGP and enable equal-cost multipath routing for them.
- C. Enable acceleration on the existing VPN connection so that the traffic uses the AWS global network and the tunnel throughput increases.
- D. Attach several VPN connections to a transit gateway that use BGP, and enable equal-cost multipath routing on the gateway.

**Answer:** D

**Explanation:** A transit gateway aggregates the bandwidth of several VPN tunnels with ECMP when the connections use dynamic routing, and it connects many VPCs; a standard tunnel carries up to 1.25 Gbps, so two connections with four tunnels cover 4 Gbps.
- Virtual private gateway: no tunnel aggregation, and one VPC only (đặt sai chỗ)
- Static routes with ECMP: ECMP is not supported with static routing (cấu hình không tồn tại)
- Acceleration: improves the network path but leaves each tunnel's throughput limit unchanged (dùng sai tính năng)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-limits.html
> 🇻🇳 Cần ~4 Gbps qua VPN tới nhiều VPC → nhiều VPN vào Transit Gateway + BGP + ECMP; VGW, route tĩnh hay acceleration không cộng gộp được băng thông.

- concept: To place compute close to users in a metro area without on-premises hardware, extend the VPC to a Local Zone; Outposts needs on-site racks, Wavelength targets 5G mobile users, and CloudFront does not cut interactive session latency
- refs: 13-other-services.md, 04-networking-services.md
- hint: Cần độ trễ một chữ số mili giây tới người dùng trong một khu vực đô thị, không có chỗ đặt rack — hạ tầng AWS nào mở rộng Region ra gần họ?
- status: draft
- created: 2026-10-22
- enriched: 2026-10-22
- time: 110

A video-production studio in Houston edits high-resolution footage in virtual workstations that run on GPU instances. The nearest AWS Region is more than 20 milliseconds away, and editors report laggy scrubbing. The studio needs single-digit millisecond latency to the workstations. It has no space for on-premises racks, wants to keep using EC2 and the AWS APIs it already uses, and keeps its projects database in the parent Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

- A. Order AWS Outposts racks for the studio's building and run the GPU workstations on them.
- B. Launch the GPU workstations in a Wavelength Zone so that the editors connect through a carrier's 5G network.
- C. Extend the VPC to an AWS Local Zone in the Houston area and run the GPU workstations and their EBS volumes there.
- D. Place the GPU workstations in the Region closest to Houston and put an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of them.

**Answer:** C

**Explanation:** A Local Zone places compute and storage close to a large population center, so a VPC subnet there gives editors low latency with the same EC2 and APIs while the database stays in the parent Region.
- Outposts racks: need physical space in the studio, which it lacks (vi phạm ràng buộc)
- Wavelength Zone: puts compute in carrier 5G networks for mobile users (dùng sai tính năng)
- CloudFront in front: caches content, so it does not shorten interactive sessions (giải bài toán khác)
Docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/local-zones/latest/ug/what-is-aws-local-zones.html
> 🇻🇳 Cần độ trễ thấp cho người dùng ở một thành phố, không có chỗ đặt rack → Local Zone (mở rộng VPC); Outposts cần rack tại chỗ, Wavelength dành cho 5G.
